messages:
maria: FYI I opened a tiny dashboard PR that adds a per-route 'bytes_in vs dims' heatmap and a small telemetry tag for 'split_count'. We should decide how the router treats mixed-dim requests once this ships. Current behavior: splitter prefers equal-dim splits which causes small, high-overhead batches. Proposal: prefer bytes-first (limit by payload bytes) and only split by dims as a last resort.

alex: link? also can you show the config you want to change? curious about edgecases where bytes-first hurts latency. :thinking_face: @maria

maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4321 (preview in the PR comment). Config snippet: 
```
route.routes["/v1/embeddings"].split_policy = "bytes_first"  # options: bytes_first | dims_first | hybrid
route.routes["/v1/embeddings"].soft_split_threshold_bytes = 512000
route.routes["/v1/embeddings"].max_split_parts = 4
```
The idea: prefer combining into byte-bounded sub-batches to avoid lots of tiny dim-only splits.

pranav: Telemetry wise we should emit: `orig_batch_dims`, `orig_batch_bytes`, `split_batches`, `split_reason` (values: bytes_overflow, dim_mismatch, tenant_softcap). Also a histogram for `post_split_tokens_per_call`. That will let us see whether bytes-first actually reduces overhead.

julie: my worry: billing/quotas. If we split server-side, do we charge per-original-request or per-split-batch? We risk confusing customers if their dashboard shows X units but billing shows Y. Need a clear rule and UI hint.

maria: good catch. Proposal: billing stays tied to original logical inputs (embedding units), console shows an "estimated server batches" column for transparency. For quota enforcement we enforce per-tenant softcaps on original logical units, but runtime may fastfail if a post-split batch exceeds hard limits.

sam: client UX angle: SDK-level preflight (opt-in header `X-Embed-Preflight: prefer`) could let clients get a suggested split plan returned with `200` and `X-Embed-Suggested-Split: parts=2;reason=bytes` so clients can decide to send pre-split payloads and avoid server splitting entirely. That would help reduce double-charging confusion.

alex: SDK preflight seems ideal for PLG users. But for server-side fallback we still need graceful behavior: options: 1) fastfail 413, ask client to retry with suggested split; 2) server-split and mark metric `server_split=true` and include `estimated_extra_bytes` so console can surface cost delta. Which do we prefer for GA?

pranav: for rollout I'd do an experiment: enable `bytes_first` in canary region + SDK preflight opt-in on 10% of tokens. Track: 95p latency, 99p latency, server_split rate, billing_delta_estimate, and 413 retry rate. If server_split rate high but billing_delta small, allow server-split.

maria: +1. I'll add a console toggle so SRE/product can flip `suggest_split` preview for a tenant and surface an "Estimated billing impact" column (small badge next to quota). Also add a telemetry panel: per-route split_reason breakdown.

julie: add a short blurb for docs and the billing page: "Server splitting does not change logical unit billing; it may increase internal GPU-side work which is shown as 'estimated server batches' in Console." That should avoid support tickets.

ingress-bot: deploy-check: route config `bytes_first` parsed OK in staging. No schema errors.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started to us-east-1 with `bytes_first` for /v1/embeddings on 10% tenants. Watchboard link: https://console.redwood.dev/splits/experiment/1751234567

maria: thanks — i'll monitor telemetry panel and post a short summary in #eng-platform after 48h. If we see >2x server_split rate vs preflight opt-in, we revert to hybrid. :wave:
